clue.text: Morecambe and Wise take acid? We could see graphic fun

parts.note: Eric Morecambe and Ernie Wise were a famous British comedy double act, so a pair of comics
to take LSD is to go on a trip

explanation.surface: A wild image of the beloved British comedy duo experimenting with LSD.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy duo of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip is a sequence of drawn panels telling a funny story, so it is humour in pictures.

clue.text: Cinders depressed by introduction to Charming's money

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Charming's
cinders are ash, the remains of a fire

explanation.surface: Cinderella is downcast at being given Prince Charming's fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinders' with its capital looks like Cinderella, but it just means ash. In a down answer, being depressed by something means sitting below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is ready money in notes and coins, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Aware of nude film Spain's banned from broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the remaining letters are strewn into a new order
what is banned is kept out, so that letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A censor, conscious of a racy film, keeps Spain from airing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the E from NUDE FILM and rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mindful of something is to be conscious of it and keep it in mind.

clue.text: Papers cutting emotional support for union

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it, splitting it in two

parts.note: consolation is comfort offered to someone upset
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Newspapers slash their sympathetic coverage, which looks like a story about a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests newspapers, but here it is identity documents, ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolidation is the joining of separate parts into one whole, a merger or union.

clue.text: Food mum has to put first and last

parts.note: taken as written, placed at the start
ma is an informal word for mother
the same word again, placed at the end

explanation.surface: A mother reminding someone to serve the meal in the right order.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'to' is used twice, once at each end of MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato is a fruit eaten as a vegetable, an example of food.

clue.text: Soldiers in cooler on crack

parts.note: taken as written
a fan is a device for cooling
to have a crack at something is to have a try

explanation.surface: Troops locked in the cooler, a military prison, for drug offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like slang for prison and 'crack' like the drug; they are a fan and an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The infantry are foot soldiers collectively, the army's fighting troops on foot.

clue.text: Try nutty rolls

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An invitation to sample some bread rolls with nuts in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty rolls' looks like baking, but nutty is the slang word for mad and rolls says turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make an attempt, so a stab is a try.

clue.text: Tango triumph raised bar, electric duo that ends with a spin

definitions.text: electric duo that ends with a spin

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a triumph is a win

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word turns it upwards so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: bar and but both mean except

explanation.surface: A dancer's tango victory lifts the bar, ending with a twirl.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin-tub is an old-style washing machine with two drums, one for washing and one that spins the clothes dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub has a pair of tubs powered by electricity, the second being a spin dryer.

clue.text: Ominously one watches great globe turning, crushing the resistance

parts.note: big means great in size

indicators.note: turning round puts a word back to front

parts.note: an orb is a globe
taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A sinister world power watches as the globe turns and resistance is crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the reversed globe sits on top of, crushing, the final THE R.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is the all-seeing leader in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, whose surveillance is menacing.

clue.text: Setter/compiler, say, that gets stuck in almost every clue

definitions.text: Setter/compiler, say, that gets stuck in almost every clue

parts.note: surface: a puzzle maker who leaves a trace in nearly every clue

parts.words: that gets stuck in almost every clue
parts.note: setter's reading: setter and compiler are words of the same meaning, and nearly every cryptic clue contains one such word as its definition

explanation.walkthrough: The slash pairs two words of identical meaning, the very relation the answer names; nearly every clue's definition is that kind of word for its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning the same as another is exactly what each clue's definition is to its answer.

clue.text: A long way north, Russian fighter's seized peasant's business?

parts.note: far means a long way

indicators.note: what has been seized is held in the grip of the captor

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A Russian jet far to the north has captured a peasant's livelihood.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that peasant's business is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants traditionally worked the land, so agriculture is their trade.

clue.text: Reform New Year promise — I've to make very small swap

indicators.note: a swap exchanges two things, so these two letters change places

parts.note: a New Year resolution is a promise made to oneself
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone vows at New Year to make a small change that will transform their life.
explanation.walkthrough: RESOLUTION plus IVE gives RESOLUTIONIVE; swapping its S and V turns it into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolutionise something is to change it radically, so reform it completely.

clue.text: One's all at sea when it comes to politics

definitions.text: One's all at sea when it comes to politics

parts.note: surface: someone confused and out of their depth
setter's reading: an elector who drifts between parties, not tied to any one, as if bobbing on the water

explanation.walkthrough: 'All at sea' means confused, but read literally it is something drifting on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An undecided elector with no fixed party loyalty is said to drift, like something adrift on the waves.

clue.text: In a different light she'd appear curvier at the bottom

indicators.note: seen in a different light, the letters take on a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A woman wonders whether different lighting would make her figure look fuller below.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped figure is wider at the hips than the shoulders, like the fruit.

clue.text: Imperial centurions in retreat, keeping food from the French?

indicators.note: a retreating army goes backwards, so the letters read right to left
the words keep the answer held within their run of letters

parts.note: the answer sits backwards across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Roman soldiers fall back, holding on to supplies seized from the Gauls.
explanation.walkthrough: The pastry runs backwards inside imperiAL CEnturions.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a French cream-filled choux pastry, so food that comes from France.

clue.text: Carpenters' number one, for instance, that's made for twisting

definitions.text: Carpenters' number one, for instance, that's made for twisting

parts.note: surface: a chart-topping hit by the pop duo the Carpenters, perhaps a song to dance the twist to
setter's reading: a woodworker's key tool, which bores holes by rotating

explanation.walkthrough: The capital C points at the 1970s pop group, but carpenters here are woodworkers and the twisting is boring holes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting piece fitted into a power tool spins to bore holes, a staple of any woodworker's kit.

clue.text: Party of three rob major in hold-up

indicators.note: in a down answer, held up means lifted to read bottom to top
the answer is contained in the run of the following words

parts.note: read backwards, the letters run through these three words

explanation.surface: A gang of three robs an army major at gunpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' looks like a robbery, which fits rob; it is the signal to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large lively celebration, a kind of party.

clue.text: Occasionally using road chart, in gear, westbound in this?

definitions.text: Occasionally using road chart, in gear, westbound in this?

indicators.note: in an across answer westward means right to left, so the letters run backwards
occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is used

parts.note: the odd letters of these words

explanation.surface: Driving a hired vehicle west now and then, map in hand and in gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the scene of a hire vehicle being driven with a road map, while also giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hire vehicle is one you might drive along with a road atlas, in gear, heading west on holiday.

clue.text: Insect heading off over Eurasian river and plain

indicators.note: with the heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a gnat is an insect; drop its first letter
the Ural river flows between Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: A bug flies off across a river on the steppe and a vast flat plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a noun for flat land, but it is the adjective meaning unadorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural and plain both describe something simple and unaffected, without artifice.

clue.text: Article, though poetically abridged, this writer must give in

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
tho' is the shortened form of though used in verse
the writer of the clue refers to themselves

explanation.surface: An author must concede to the editor that a piece of verse needs cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give in' reads as surrender; split it, and 'in' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in means being at home, not out of the house.

clue.text: Bonus I'm getting together in big collection

indicators.note: the letters are gathered and combined afresh into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates getting a bonus from joining a large compilation.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition gathers several works into one large volume.

clue.text: Danger signals as Capone maybe tools up

parts.note: Al Capone, the gangster, is an example of an Al
to tool up is slang for to arm oneself

explanation.surface: Warning bells ring as the gangster gets his guns ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarms are warning sounds that alert people to danger.

clue.text: Vehicle that gets blown up, in more ways than one

definitions.text: Vehicle that gets blown up, in more ways than one

parts.note: surface: a car destroyed by a bomb
setter's reading: a craft inflated with heated gas, which also rises up on the wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' suggests an explosion, but here it means inflated and also carried aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: This aircraft is filled by blasting heated gas into its envelope, then floats upward.

clue.text: Fly-by-nights slow dancing

indicators.note: dancers move about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Untrustworthy types doing a slow dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly-by-night is usually an unreliable person; read literally, it is something that flies by night.
explanation.definitionFit: These birds are nocturnal hunters, literally flying through the night.

clue.text: Slash and Eminem's music upset wife?

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a slash is a tear or rent
Eminem is a rap artist

explanation.surface: Guitarist Slash and rapper Eminem have offended someone's wife with their music.
explanation.walkthrough: Slash is the Guns N' Roses guitarist, but here it means a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife is one example of a partner; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Sky's most colourful show?

parts.note: surface: Sky, the British satellite TV broadcaster
setter's reading: the bright arc of colours displayed in the heavens after rain

explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British TV company, which makes 'show' look like a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of seven colours in the heavens is literally the brightest display the sky puts on.

clue.text: Shop's place to find curry, not hot

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Delhi is an Indian city, home of curry
H is the abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A shop sells curry that is mild rather than spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: Concerned with stubborn females becoming judges again?

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a stubborn person is an ass, and the suffix -ess makes female forms as in lioness, so a jokey plural for female asses

explanation.surface: Pig-headed women turning into judges for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: ass plus the feminine ending -ess, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate something once more, so to judge it again.
